title: This Border Marker Sits 370 m Off the 49th Parallel #shorts
summary: Boundary monument 347 on the Alberta-Montana line sits about 370 m south of 49°N (our calculation from the official listing); the border runs straight between monuments, and a 2002 Washington ruling followed the border as marked.
tags: why is the us canada border straight
sources: The 49th parallel east of the Rockies was originally surveyed during the years 1872 to 1875; latitude determined by astronomic observations at about 32-kilometre (20-mile) intervals; the prairie section resurveyed, mapped and monumented 1909-1912 (International Boundary Commission, Section E, Gulf of Georgia to the Northwesternmost Point of Lake of the Woods): https://internationalboundarycommission.org/en/maps-coordinates/maps/section-e.php

Monument 347 (Alberta/Montana): N 48 59 48.0, W 111 34 32.5 (NAD83, averaged grid shift; NAD27 N 48 59 48.04); neighbouring monuments 343-351 used for the drawn chain. 12.0 seconds of latitude south of 49 N at about 30.9 m per second = about 370 m (Map Minutes calculation from the official listing, which is for information only and not the legal definition) (International Boundary Commission, 49th Parallel AB-SK-MB/MT-ND geographical coordinates listing): https://www.internationalboundarycommission.org/uploads/maps/21-49th_parallel_prairies/49th%20parallel%20ab_sk_mb-mt_nd%20(english).pdf

Treaty of 24 February 1925, Article II: the boundary along the 49th parallel shall be defined as consisting of a series of right or straight lines joining adjacent monuments, replacing the definition under which the line between monuments had the curvature of the parallel (Foreign Relations of the United States 1925, Office of the Historian): https://history.state.gov/historicaldocuments/frus1925v01/d387

State v. Norman, 145 Wn.2d 578 (Washington Supreme Court, 21 February 2002): 'We hold that this state's northern boundary is coextensive with the international boundary as marked'; the border does not lie on the 49th parallel as currently located; customs sites lay north of the parallel but south of the border; in the 1858-1862 survey the English Commissioner reported errors 'as great as 860 feet and none less than 180 feet' between the Similkameen and the Kettle River when US and British points were linked, attributed to local deflection of the plumb line and resolved by running a mean parallel; the boundary between marks was agreed to be a straight line (FindLaw): https://caselaw.findlaw.com/wa-supreme-court/1329211.html

Map data: Natural Earth (public domain) https://www.naturalearthdata.com and US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain) https://www.census.gov/geographies/mapping-files/time-series/geo/carto-boundary-file.html

scenes.narration: This border marker in Alberta sits about {370 m|three hundred and seventy metres} south of the {49th|forty-ninth} parallel.
It's monument {347|three forty-seven}. Between markers, the border runs in straight lines.
In {2002|two thousand two}, Washington's Supreme Court ruled the state ends at the border as marked, not at the parallel.

data.source: State v. Norman, Washington Supreme Court, 2002

scenes.narration: So the border isn't exactly the {49th|forty-ninth} parallel. It's wherever the markers stand.
